title: Validate synchronous grant liveness at every I/O
summary: Issuer identity and a current scope are insufficient after the issuing callback ends; check private liveness on every use.
reusable_steps: Issuer identity and a current scope are insufficient after the issuing callback ends; check private liveness on every use
expected_outcome: Keep each domain's opaque grant issuer private. Bind its token to the exact frozen resource scope in an issuer-local registry and require the same current execution scope at each I/O. Revoke in finally, reject asynchronous callbacks and escaped grant material, and intersect enclosing resource ceilings. A queued callback may retain an async-local scope object after the synchronous issuer has finished; object identity alone must not admit its read. Validate liveness again at the secure I/O boundary. Keep actual principal, tenant, broker and egress authorization in existing domain facades rather than treating the shared mechanism or a catalog entry as authority. The credential regression checks denied admission after the callback, not a demonstrated leak of secret bytes.
